atharobari-zamindar-bari.desc: Atharobari is a village in Ishwarganj upazila, and it takes its name from the zamindar house that still stands there. The estate's old buildings are a reminder of the landed families who once ran much of greater Mymensingh. Few outsiders come here, so you are likely to have the place to yourself, apart from curious villagers.
blocks: How to get there
From Mymensingh take a bus or CNG to Ishwarganj, then a CNG or auto to Atharobari village.
Good to know
Parts of the old buildings may be fragile or in private use; ask before entering.

glance: 110 km to Mymensingh by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
alexander-castle-mymensingh.desc: Built in 1879 by Maharaja Suryakanta Acharya Chowdhury, the building was named after Alexandra, then Princess of Wales. Its walls use iron sheeting in places, which gave it the local nickname 'Lohar Kuthi'. Rabindranath Tagore, Mahatma Gandhi and other figures are said to have stayed here. It now lies inside the grounds of a teachers' training college, so ask permission to look around.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw to the Teachers' Training College in Mymensingh town.
Good to know
It is on college grounds; visit during working hours and ask at the gate.

glance: 110 km to Mymensingh by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
kadigarh-national-park.desc: Kadigarh National Park covers about 344 hectares of sal forest in Bhaluka upazila, in the south of Mymensingh district. It was declared a national park in October 2010 and sits roughly a kilometre north of Kachina bazar on the Siddhastor–Sakhipur road. Paths lead under the tall sal trees, and the forest is quiet compared with the busier parks closer to Dhaka. Illegal logging by sawmills in surrounding villages is a real threat, so what you see is a forest under pressure.
blocks: How to get there
Take a Mymensingh-bound bus to Bhaluka, then a CNG toward Siddhastor and Kachina bazar; the forest starts just north of the bazar.
Good to know
Go in a group or with a local, as there are few facilities and the paths are not marked. Carry water.

zainul-abedin-museum-riverside.desc: Zainul Abedin, whose sketches of the 1943 Bengal famine made him famous, grew up by the Brahmaputra and painted it often. His museum on the riverbank in Mymensingh town holds a collection of his paintings and sketches. Outside, the riverside park is a favourite walking spot, and boats cross to the sandbanks on the far side. Late afternoon light on the river is lovely.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw to Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin Park on the riverbank.
Good to know
The museum has a weekly closing day; check before going.

glance: 110 km to Mymensingh by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
nazrul-smriti-kendra-trishal.desc: As a teenager Kazi Nazrul Islam lived in Trishal and studied at the Darirampur school, and the upazila has kept that link alive ever since. The Nazrul Smriti Kendra is a memorial museum with photographs, documents and other material about the poet's life and his time in Trishal. The national university named after him, Jatiya Kabi Kazi Nazrul Islam University, is also in Trishal, so the town makes an easy stop on the Dhaka–Mymensingh highway.
blocks: How to get there
Any Dhaka–Mymensingh bus can drop you at Trishal; from there take a rickshaw or auto to the memorial. From Mymensingh town it is under an hour.
Good to know
Check opening days locally before making a special trip. Combine it with a walk around the Nazrul University campus.

nandail-chyapa-shutki.desc: Chyapa (also called sidol or hidol in this region) is made from small puti fish that are cleaned, lightly sun-dried and packed into earthen pots, often buried, to ferment for months. The result is strong-smelling and deeply savoury, and it is mashed into fiery bhorta or cooked with onion and chilli. Greater Mymensingh and the haor belt are its heartland. In Nandail, makers such as Hasu Mia of Savar village sell their chyapa at the municipal market three days a week, and buyers come from other districts.
blocks: Good to know
The smell is strong; ask for it well sealed if you are carrying it on a bus.

glance: Growers and bazaars in Fulbaria upazila, such as around Palashtoli village, and shops in Mymensingh town
fulbaria-lal-chini.desc: Farmers in villages of Fulbaria upazila boil fresh sugarcane juice and work it by hand into a fine-grained, reddish-brown sugar, without machines or chemicals. Locals date the craft to the British period, roughly two and a half centuries back. It is used in sherbet, pitha and home sweets and has a deeper, molasses-like taste than white sugar. Fulbaria's lal chini received Geographical Indication status in 2025.

glance: 110 km to Mymensingh by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
bau-botanical-garden.desc: Bangladesh Agricultural University, founded in 1961, has one of the greenest campuses in the country, stretching along the Old Brahmaputra. Its botanical garden holds a large collection of native and exotic plants, and experimental fields and ponds fill much of the grounds. The riverside road on campus is a peaceful place to walk or cycle. Students and locals gather at the riverbank in the evening.
blocks: How to get there
Auto or rickshaw from Mymensingh town, about 15 minutes.
Good to know
Respect university rules; some areas may be restricted to visitors.

mymensingh-river-fish.desc: Mymensingh, especially around Trishal and Muktagacha, is the centre of Bangladesh's fish farming, with thousands of ponds supplying Dhaka and beyond. Pangas, tilapia, rui and koi are cheap and very fresh here. Town eateries cook them in spicy bhuna and light jhol, alongside small fish from the Brahmaputra. It is a good place to try a full Bengali fish lunch.

mymensingh-malaikari.desc: Malaikari is made by cutting a round ball of chhana in half and spreading thick milk kheer over the cut faces. The story in town is that Janaki Nag's sweet shop in Swadeshi Bazar, said to be Mymensingh's first sweet shop, created it about a hundred years ago for a shraddha hosted by the Muktagacha zamindar, who wanted something new. It stayed on the menu and spread across the city. Krishna Cabin, open since 1958, also makes it and supplies sweet sellers in Mymensingh and Netrokona.

muktagacha-rajbari.desc: The Acharya Chowdhury family of Muktagacha were among the most powerful zamindars of Mymensingh. Their palace complex includes residential blocks, temples, a ruined throne room and ornamented gateways, some restored and some crumbling. Walking through the courtyards gives a sense of how big these estates were. After visiting, walk to the monda shop in town.
blocks: How to get there
Bus or CNG from Mymensingh town to Muktagacha, about 30–40 minutes.
Good to know
Some parts are unsafe; avoid entering decaying buildings.

glance: Gopal Pal's shop in Muktagacha town
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
muktagacha-monda.desc: Monda is a soft, slightly grainy disc of chhana and sugar, less syrupy than most Bengali sweets. The shop founded by Gopal Pal in Muktagacha in 1824 still makes it, and his descendants keep the recipe a family secret. Local stories say it was served to zamindars and visiting dignitaries. Eat one at the shop and take a box home.

mymensingh-gitika.desc: In the early 20th century, Chandra Kumar De collected ballads sung by villagers of greater Mymensingh, and Dinesh Chandra Sen published them as the Mymensingh Gitika. Stories such as Mahua and Malua tell of love, caste and fate, often with strong women at their centre. The ballads have been translated into many languages and are staged as plays and dance. Local cultural groups still perform them at fairs and festivals.

glance: 110 km to Mymensingh by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
shashi-lodge.desc: Shashi Lodge was built by the Muktagacha zamindar Suryakanta Acharya Chowdhury and rebuilt by his adopted son Shashikanta after the 1897 earthquake. The two-storey building has a long colonnaded front, coloured glass and a garden with a fountain topped by a marble Venus. It later housed a women's teacher training college and has since been taken over for use as a museum. The garden is a pleasant place to sit in the afternoon.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw from anywhere in Mymensingh town.
Good to know
Check opening days and hours locally before visiting.
